list.name: baseline
list.label: Baseline sweep
list.definition:
SELECT sweep_name AS __text, sweep_name AS __value
FROM bench.sweeps
WHERE is_complete AND NOT is_flagged_invalid AND derived_from IS NULL
ORDER BY captured_at DESC;

panels.title: Flip table — per-query pass counts, baseline vs candidate
panels.description: All-time corpus; the two sweeps come from the baseline and candidate variables, not the time picker. Per-query pass counts for the two selected sweeps. This is the panel that turns "26 of 30" into "q01 broke" — which is the difference between knowing a change regressed and knowing what it regressed. Incomplete, INVALID-flagged and re-costed sweeps are kept out of both selectors.

targets.rawSql:
WITH base AS (
    SELECT query_id,
           count(*) AS n,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') AS passed
    FROM bench.runs
    WHERE sweep_name = ${baseline:sqlstring}
    GROUP BY query_id
),
cand AS (
    SELECT query_id,
           count(*) AS n,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed') AS passed
    FROM bench.runs
    WHERE sweep_name = ${candidate:sqlstring}
    GROUP BY query_id
)
SELECT base.query_id                                  AS "query",
       base.passed || '/' || base.n                   AS "baseline",
       cand.passed || '/' || cand.n                   AS "candidate",
       cand.passed - base.passed                      AS "delta",
       CASE
           WHEN cand.passed < base.passed THEN 'BROKE'
           WHEN cand.passed > base.passed THEN 'FIXED'
           ELSE ''
       END                                            AS "verdict"
FROM base
LEFT JOIN cand ON cand.query_id = base.query_id
ORDER BY "delta" ASC, base.query_id;

panels.title: Gate row — pass %, locator success, flake minus repairs
panels.description: All-time; follows the sweep selectors, not the time picker. Three gate metrics, not four. Planner salvage is NOT here and cannot be: there is no salvage column in any of the four CSV header shapes, no salvage field on the metrics model, and no guardrail span in llm_traces. It is a log-only signal and stays a manual check. Saying so beats rendering a silent 0, which would be exactly the kind of quiet wrong answer the blank-dryrun rule exists to prevent. The standing gate is pass rate at or above 96.7%, locator success 1.0, and flake minus repairs 0.

targets.rawSql:
WITH pair AS (
    SELECT CASE WHEN sweep_name = ${baseline:sqlstring} THEN 'baseline'
                ELSE 'candidate' END AS arm,
           test_status, locator_success_rate, flake_retries, dryrun_repairs
    FROM bench.runs
    WHERE sweep_name IN (${baseline:sqlstring}, ${candidate:sqlstring})
)
SELECT arm                                                             AS "arm",
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE test_status = 'passed')
             / count(*), 1)                                            AS "pass %",
       round(avg(locator_success_rate)::numeric, 4)                    AS "locator success",
       sum(flake_retries) - sum(dryrun_repairs)                        AS "flake - repairs"
FROM pair
GROUP BY arm
ORDER BY arm;

panels.title: Reproducibility — observed spread across same-code repeats
panels.description: All-time. Every deliberate same-code repeat in the corpus, shown beside the candidate delta so a reader can see the comparison's resolution: 25/30 vs 25/30, 30/30 vs 30/30, and 29/30 vs 30/30. n=3 is the entire evidence base for reproducibility. The 2.40 standard deviation across 53 clean complete public sweeps is NOT a noise floor — it spans a month in which the code genuinely improved from 22/30 to 30/30. The experiment that would close this: run one commit twice and record the pair.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'observed |delta| across same-code repeat pairs' AS "measure",
       '0, 0, +1 (n=3)'                                 AS "value";

panels.title: Cost, tokens and latency — baseline vs candidate
panels.description: All-time; follows the sweep selectors, not the time picker. Two standing caveats apply and neither is defensible to ignore. Timing is comparable only within a session — Vertex latency swung from 0.76s to 18.2s inside one day — so a latency delta between sweeps run on different days measures the provider, not the change. Cost swings on the Gemini implicit-cache lottery by around 2% per run, enough to flip a verdict from +7.3% to -1.3%, so never gate on one run. There is deliberately no 429-based trust flag: 32 of the 78 sweeps do not carry llm_429_count at all, and across the 46 that do it correlates at r = +0.29 with pass count — positive, meaning sweeps with more 429s scored slightly better, which is confounding by time rather than a signal. The one sweep manually flagged INVALID at 3/30 recorded an unremarkable 4.

targets.rawSql:
WITH pair AS (
    SELECT CASE WHEN sweep_name = ${baseline:sqlstring} THEN 'baseline'
                ELSE 'candidate' END AS arm,
           llm_cost_usd, llm_tokens, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_s
    FROM bench.runs
    WHERE sweep_name IN (${baseline:sqlstring}, ${candidate:sqlstring})
)
SELECT arm                                              AS "arm",
       round(avg(llm_cost_usd)::numeric, 4)             AS "median-ish cost $",
       round(avg(llm_tokens)::numeric, 0)               AS "avg tokens",
       round(avg(prompt_tokens)::numeric, 0)            AS "avg prompt",
       round(avg(completion_tokens)::numeric, 0)        AS "avg completion",
       round(avg(total_s)::numeric, 1)                  AS "avg total s"
FROM pair
GROUP BY arm
ORDER BY arm;
